candidates.title: Windmill Exercise for Core and Back Strength -MoveU
candidates.description:
Start Fixin Yo’ Sh!T - https://MoveU.com

Lower back strengthening is one of the best things you can do for back pain. The Windmill exercise is an awesome “twist” on the traditional straight-leg deadlift. The target muscles for this exercise are the hamstrings, glutes, obliques, and quadratus lumborum in the lower back (painted on me).

This exercise is super fun and a little challenging. If you have never done this movement, do it without weight at first. If you have tight hamstrings, you may need to have a wider stance than I do in the video. Start with your feet turned in the same direction that you are going to bend over. Make sure your hips are pointed straight forward though. From there, sit your butt back and to the side, not straight back. As you hinge over, reach your bottom hand for your knee/lower-leg/foot without rounding the lower back. The Quadratus Lumborum will activate and prevent the spine from rounding. This is more of an “isometric” movement for the lower back. 

You should feel a big stretch in the hamstring of the leg that you are leaning toward. Hinge over as far as you can without your lower back rounding, then squeeze the glute and hamstrings and thrust your pelvis forward to stand up.

Watch the top hand the entire time if you are using a weight. Watching the weight helps you keep it under control. To challenge yourself, don’t watch the weight, but this is much more advanced.

candidates.title: How To Perform and Master the Kettlebell Windmill Exercise
candidates.description:
Discover the 7 Best Kettlebell Ab Exercises here: https://kettlebellsworkouts.com/kettlebell-ab-exercises/

Kettlebell Windmills are another good all over body exercise using the kettlebell. Just like the Turkish Get Up they primarily improve your mobility and stability of your shoulders, and hips.

Getting good at the Windmill will help improve your hip mobility by loosening off your hamstrings and will also help mobilise and strengthen your shoulders.

Again the abs get a great workout during the Windmill. The obliques in particular get targeted as you rotate your body during the downward movement as well as when you return to the upright position.

The Windmill is a slow exercise so take your time, 5 seconds or more is a standard tempo for the exercise. Work on getting deep into the movement as you progress and keep that core nice and tight throughout the movement.

candidates.title: Kettlebell Windmill
candidates.description:
The kettlebell windmill exercise is an advanced kettlebell movement that challenges muscles of the shoulders, strengthens the core, glutes, and hamstrings, and improves overall joint mobility.

How to:
1. Turn your feet 45 degrees opposite the KB in hand
2. Open your palm up and slide it down the leg opposite of the KB in hand
3. Stack the KB directly on top of the elbow and shoulder
4. Maintain a neutral spine by turning your head to look at the KB
5. Hinge at the hips keeping your knees ina slight bent position
6. Stick your butt out and slide your palm down until you cannot hinge any further
